missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Nominative subject. 'Ужин' is a masculine noun in the nominative case, the subject of the sentence. 'Готов' is the short-form adjective agreeing in the masculine, and 'почти' softens it.
Strategic focus: Accusative object. 'Ужин' is an inanimate masculine noun, so its accusative matches the nominative as the object of 'приготовила'. 'Вкусный' agrees in the masculine accusative.
Strategic focus: Genitive after предлог. 'Ужина' is the genitive form after 'после', marking the time after dinner. 'Чай' is the accusative object of 'пили'.
Strategic focus: Dative after предлог. 'Ужину' is the dative form after 'к', expressing the occasion they arrived for. 'Гости' is the nominative plural subject of 'пришли'.
Strategic focus: Instrumental after довольны. 'Ужином' is the instrumental form required by the adjective 'довольны', which always governs the instrumental. The phrase expresses satisfaction.
Strategic focus: Prepositional location. 'Ужине' is the prepositional form after 'на', describing where there were many dishes. 'Блюд' is genitive plural after 'много'.
Strategic focus: Nominative plural subject. 'Ужины' is the nominative plural, the subject of 'проходят'. 'Семейные' agrees in the plural, and 'весело' describes how they go.
Strategic focus: Accusative plural object. 'Ужины' is the accusative plural, identical to the nominative for inanimate nouns, the object of 'предлагает'. 'Романтические' agrees in the plural.
Strategic focus: Genitive after отрицание. 'Ужина' is the genitive form required after the negation 'нет', expressing the absence of dinner. 'У нас' marks whose dinner is missing.
Strategic focus: Instrumental after предлог. 'Ужином' is the instrumental form after 'перед', meaning before dinner. 'Руки' is the accusative plural object of 'вымыл'.
